```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(chromatographR)
data("Sa_warp")
```


```{r get_peaktable}
pks <- get_peaks(Sa_warp, lambdas = 210)
pktab <- get_peaktable(pks)
```

```{r attach_reference_spectra}
pktab <- attach_ref_spectra(pktab, ref = "max.cor")
```

After assigning reference spectra to our peak table, we can use Pearson correlations to locate peaks within a chosen similarity threshold of a reference spectrum. To do this, we first construct a correlation matrix using the `cor` function.

##### Analysis of spectral correlations

```{r make_correlation_matrix}
cor_mat <- cor(pktab$ref_spectra)
```

We can then plot spectra falling within a desired similarity threshold (`t`) to a reference peak (in this case `V18`).

```{r plot_spectra}
ref <- "V18"
wl <- as.numeric(rownames(pktab$ref_spectra))
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
idx_90 <- which(cor_mat[,ref] > .9)
matplot(wl, pktab$ref_spectra[,idx_90], type='l',
        xlab="Wavelength (nm)", ylab="Relative absorbance")
legend("top", "t = 0.90", bty = "n")

idx_95 <- which(cor_mat[,ref] > .95)
matplot(wl, pktab$ref_spectra[,idx_95], type='l',
        xlab="Wavelength (nm)", ylab="Relative absorbance")
legend("top", "t = 0.95", bty = "n")

idx_97 <- which(cor_mat[,ref] > .97)
matplot(wl, pktab$ref_spectra[,idx_97], type='l',
        xlab="Wavelength (nm)", ylab="Relative absorbance")
legend("top", "t = 0.97", bty = "n")

idx_99 <- which(cor_mat[,ref] > .99)
matplot(wl, pktab$ref_spectra[,idx_99], type='l',
        xlab="Wavelength (nm)", ylab="Relative absorbance")
legend("top", "t = 0.99", bty = "n")
```

We can also extract retention times for spectra above the desired spectral similarity threshold with the reference spectra.

```{r get_retention_times}
rts_99 = pktab$pk_meta["rt", idx_99]
rts_99
```

Below we plot traces of our four chromatograms at 210 nm. The `r length(idx_99)` peaks that match the reference spectrum at the 99% level are marked with solid black lines and the `r length(idx_97)` peaks that match the reference spectrum at the 97% level are marked with dotted gray lines.

```{r plot_chroms}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
plot_chroms(Sa_warp, lambdas=210)

abline(v = rts_99)
abline(v = pktab$pk_meta["rt", idx_97], lty=2, col = "darkgray")
```

If we are interested in the combined area of these peaks, we could also use these indices to sum them together.

```{r sum_areas}
rowSums(pktab$tab[, idx_99, drop = FALSE])
```

##### Hierarchical clustering of spectra

`chromatographR` also includes a function (`cluster_spectra`) to group spectra using hierarchical clustering. We can set the seed with the `iseed` argument to ensure repeatability among instantiations of this vignette. Clusters of 20 or more peaks span most of the table and say little about any one chromophore, so we drop them with `max_size`.

```{r hierarchical_clustering}
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
cl <- cluster_spectra(pktab, alpha = 0.05, max_size = 20, iseed = 1)
```

The output is a dendrogram of peaks, annotated with bootstrap values (cluster support estimated by resampling) at each node. It also plots the spectra of clusters whose bootstrap p-value falls below the significance level specified by `alpha`. In this case, we recovered `r length(cl$clusters)` clusters. We can find the cluster containing our reference peak and access its peaks as follows:

```{r return_peaks}
ref_cl <- Filter(function(k) ref %in% k@peaks, cl$clusters)[[1]]
ref_cl@peaks
```

This cluster holds the same peaks that correlate with `r ref` above 0.95:

```{r show_overlap}
setequal(ref_cl@peaks, names(idx_95))
```
